claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

First, let me start with a basic question:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask you some questions about Alex to determine his eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he at school, college, sixth form, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school but he's not studying anything right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have a few more questions about Alex's situation:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?** If so, when did he leave education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or anything like that. He just left school and has been at home since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently working?** If so, how many hours per week does he work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex currently claiming any benefits in his own right**, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

Since Alex is 17 years old, he falls into the 16-19 age group where Child Benefit eligibility requires that the child stays in approved education or training. Alex has left school and is not currently in any approved education or training program.

There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks if a 16 or 17-year-old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, but Alex has not done this either.

**What this means:**
- If you were previously receiving Child Benefit for Alex, it should have stopped when he left education and did not continue into approved training
- You cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex in his current situation

**Possible next steps for Alex:**
If Alex were to enroll in approved education or training, or register with a government-sponsored careers service, you might be able to claim Child Benefit again. If his circumstances change, you would need to inform HMRC.
